mainTopic: Witnesses fit at the start and end; when a poor person counts as rich for קרבנות; and the rules of age, gender and timing for ערכין
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא: a witness who was fit when he saw the event and fit when he testifies is כשר, even if he was unfit in between. The גמרא explains that testimony depends only on seeing and telling. It then shows that the word והוא teaches something else: witnesses are only liable for a שבועת העדות if they were singled out. Next the גמרא explains the משנה's rule that a poor מצורע stays poor for his קרבנות even when money is coming to him. In one case his father is a גוסס. In the other, his ship is rented out, the rent comes only at the end, and, following רבי אליעזר, his work tools are not counted. A new משנה teaches that a ערך follows the age and gender of the person being valued, and his age at the time of the vow. A פסוק supports the timing rule. Another משנה rules that the boundary years count with the younger age group, learned through a מופנה גזירה שוה of 'שנה'. Finally the גמרא asks whether this fits רבי, who holds that 'עד' includes the endpoint, and begins quoting his source about the days of פסח, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A witness who was unfit only in the middle is still valid
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists witnesses who were fit at the start, became unfit, and became fit again, and rules they are כשר. Its rule is that if the beginning and end are fit, the witness is fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...and afterward his daughter died. Or he could hear, became a חרש, and could hear again. Or he could see, became blind, and then could see again. Or he was sane, became a שוטה, and became sane again. In all these cases he is fit. This is the rule: anyone whose beginning and end are in a fit state is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא about witnesses whose status changed in the middle. The ברייתא says they can still testify if they were fit at the start and at the end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case has the same pattern: fit, then unfit, then fit again. The ברייתא says the middle does not matter. This seems to go against reading והוא עד as "he must be the same fit person the whole time," so the ברייתא works as a challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: A deaf-mute. Treated as not able to testify.
A blind person. Cannot testify about what he saw while blind.
A person who is not mentally competent.
Fit or valid (here: fit to testify).
"This is the rule." Sums up all the cases in one principle.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the start of the ברייתא. Its opening (about becoming a son-in-law) came just before this line. "His daughter" means the daughter of the person in the case, who was the witness's wife.

phrases.english: and afterward his daughter died,
phrases.notes: His daughter was the witness's wife, so once she died, the witness is no longer his relative.

phrases.english: he could hear and became deaf,
and then could hear again;
he could see and became blind,
and afterward could see again;
he was sane and became insane,
and then became sane again: he is fit.
This is the rule:
anyone whose beginning and end are in a fit state is fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה הַכְּלָל: כֹּל שֶׁתְּחִילָּתוֹ וְסוֹפוֹ בְּכַשְׁרוּת — כָּשֵׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא that started before this section and was brought to challenge the reading of והוא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that והוא עד requires the witness to be fit from beginning to end with no break.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא accepts a witness who was unfit in the middle. So והוא cannot mean the witness must stay fit the entire time.

steps.title: Testimony depends only on seeing and telling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that witnesses are different. The פסוק ties testimony to seeing and telling, and both happened while he was fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the פסוק says, "or he saw... if he does not tell." The Torah made the matter depend on seeing and telling, and here we have both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It says the rule for witnesses comes from a different part of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names two moments: when the witness sees and when he tells. A witness who was fit at both moments meets what the תורה requires, so the middle period does not matter. This means the ברייתא does not prove anything about how to read והוא.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is different there." Sets that case apart from the general rule.
The פסוק (verse).
Seeing the event and telling it in court.
"The Merciful One." A name for ה׳ as the Giver of the תורה.

phrases.english: It is different there,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר קְרָא: ״אוֹ רָאָה... אִם לֹא יַגִּיד״,
phrases.english: because the verse says: "or he saw... if he does not tell,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:1

phrases.english: on seeing and telling
the Merciful One made the matter depend,
and here there is both.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Sets the case apart: witnesses have their own source in the words ראה and יגיד.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to prove that והוא does not require being fit from beginning to end.
steps.terutzMaskana: For witnesses, only seeing and telling count. So the ברייתא says nothing about the meaning of והוא.

steps.title: Then why does the פסוק say "and he"?
steps.stepSummary: If seeing and telling are all that matter, the word והוא seems to be extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, why do I need the word "and he"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. If the witness rule comes from seeing and telling, the word והוא seems to have nothing to teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes no word in the תורה is extra. Once והוא is not needed for "fit from beginning to end" when it comes to witnesses, it has to teach something else. This sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: "But then..." Opens a pushback against what was just said.
"Why do I need it?" Asks why a word is in the פסוק.
"And he." The word in the פסוק being discussed.

phrases.english: But then why do I need "and he"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 2 by asking what the word והוא is for.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the witness rule comes only from ראה and יגיד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that answer is right, the word והוא in the same פסוק seems to have no job.

steps.title: "And he" means the witnesses must be singled out
steps.stepSummary: והוא teaches that witnesses are not liable for a שבועת העדות if the person spoke to a whole crowd without singling them out.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for what was taught in a ברייתא: A man saw a group of people standing, with his witnesses among them. He said, "I make you swear: if you know any testimony for me, come and testify for me." You might think they would be liable. So the פסוק says "and he is a witness," and here he did not single out his witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that והוא has its own lesson, and brings a ברייתא to show it. Witnesses who were asked only as part of a general crowd are not liable for a שבועת העדות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "he" points to a specific person. So the oath only applies when the witness himself was singled out. Making a whole crowd swear is too general, so the witnesses in it are not liable for the קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: A group or crowd of people.
An oath about testimony. A witness who falsely swears he knows no testimony brings a קרבן.
"I make you swear." The words that put someone under oath.
"You might think." Sets up an idea the פסוק will reject.
"So the פסוק says." Brings the verse that settles the question.
He singled out his witnesses.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a practical rule for שבועת העדות: the oath must be aimed at specific witnesses, not at the public in general.

phrases.english: It is needed for that which was taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: רָאָה סִיאָה שֶׁל בְּנֵי אָדָם עוֹמְדִין,
phrases.english: if someone saw a group of people standing,
and his witnesses were among them,
and he said: "I make you swear
that if you know testimony for me
you will come and testify for me,"
you might think they would be liable?
phrases.notes: Liable to bring a קרבן if they falsely swore they knew nothing.

phrases.english: So the verse says: "and he is a witness,"
and here he did not single out his witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 3 about what והוא is for.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the word והוא is needed.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It teaches that witnesses are only liable for a שבועת העדות when they were singled out, not when they were addressed as part of a general crowd.

steps.title: Saying "whoever" does count as singling out
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: if he said "whoever knows," that does count as singling out the witnesses, so they are liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think that even if he said "whoever among you knows," they would not be liable. So the פסוק says "and he is a witness," and here he did single out his witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by setting the limit of the rule. Speaking to "whoever" knows testimony counts as singling out the witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Whoever" points to the specific people who actually know the testimony, not to the crowd as a whole. So it counts as singling them out, and they are liable. This gives והוא a clear job, which answers the question from step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: "Whoever." Here: whoever among you knows testimony for me.
"And here..." Applies the rule to the case.
Liable (here: to bring the קרבן for a false oath).

steps.whatToRemember: Witnesses count as fit if they were fit when they saw and when they tell, because the תורה ties testimony to seeing and telling. The word והוא teaches something else: a שבועת העדות only binds witnesses who were singled out. Speaking to a general crowd does not count, but saying "whoever knows" does.
steps.confusionAlert: The difference between the two cases is about who is being spoken to, not about how many people are there. "All of you" is aimed at the crowd, while "whoever knows" is aimed at the actual witnesses.

phrases.english: You might think the same even if he said "whoever"?
phrases.notes: He means: "Whoever knows testimony for me, come and testify."

phrases.english: So the verse says: "and he is a witness,"
and here he did single out his witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and sets the limit of the rule from step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Saying "whoever" counts as singling out the witnesses, so they are liable.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: והוא עד requires the witnesses to be singled out. A general crowd is not singled out, but "whoever knows" is.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about קרבנות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line of the משנה that says קרבנות work differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: but with קרבנות it is not so, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה so it can start asking about it. This is a setup line for the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that with קרבנות, a poor person brings a poor man's קרבן based on what he has now. Money that is only coming to him later, like an inheritance or a ship's cargo, does not make him rich. The 'וכו׳' points to those cases, which the גמרא will now ask about one by one.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings; here, the offerings a מצורע brings, which change depending on whether he is rich or poor
'And so on'; the rest of the quoted line is assumed

phrases.english: But with the offerings it is not so, etc.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה about the קרבנות of a poor מצורע.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: explaining a line from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For קרבנות, a poor person's status is not changed by money that has not yet reached him.

steps.title: If his father already died and left him money, he is rich
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the משנה can call him poor if his father has already died and left him ten thousand.
steps.simpleTranslation: His father died and left him ten thousand? Then he is rich!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges one case in the משנה. Someone who has already inherited ten thousand is rich, so why call him poor?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the father dies, the money belongs to the son right away. So the wording 'his father died and left him' seems to describe a rich person, not a poor one.

keyTerms.meaning: Ten thousand (dinars), a large sum
Rich; someone who must bring the rich man's קרבן

phrases.english: His father died and left him ten thousand —
he is rich!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the משנה just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's case of 'his father died and left him ten thousand'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An inheritance that has already happened makes him rich now, so he cannot be called poor.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: read it as 'is about to leave him'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו changes the reading: the father is about to leave him the money but has not died yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: Say instead, 'is leaving him ten thousand.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers by changing how we read the משנה. The father has not died yet; he is only about to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By changing the past tense 'left him' into 'is leaving him,' the money has not reached the son yet. So the son really is poor right now, and the problem goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Say instead'; a sign that the wording is being read differently
Is leaving (present tense), meaning he has not died yet

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said: Say instead:
he is leaving him ten thousand.
phrases.notes: The father is still alive. The money is coming but has not arrived.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The father already died, so the son is rich.
steps.terutzMaskana: The father is still alive and the money is only expected, so the son is poor now.

steps.title: Then it is obvious
steps.stepSummary: If the father is still alive, it is obvious the son is poor, so why does the משנה need to say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: That's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי אבהו's reading. If the son has no money yet, of course he is poor, so what is the משנה teaching?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה is not supposed to teach something everyone already knows. The new reading seems to make the line pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It's obvious!'; a challenge that a teaching adds nothing new

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אבהו's answer from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's reading 'he is leaving him'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the money has not come yet, of course he is poor. The משנה would be teaching nothing new.

steps.title: The father is a גוסס, and most גוססין die
steps.stepSummary: The case is a father who is a גוסס. We might have thought the son already counts as rich since most גוססין die, so the משנה teaches that he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is when his father was a גוסס. You might have said that most גוססין die, so he already counts as rich. So the משנה teaches us that he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the teaching is not obvious. The father is about to die, and we might have treated the son as rich already.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since most people who are גוסס end up dying, we might have counted the money as good as his. The משנה teaches that until the father actually dies, the son stays poor for his קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: A person in the last stage before death
Majority; what usually happens
'You might have said'; introduces the mistaken idea we could have had
'It teaches us'; shows what new point the source is making

steps.whatToRemember: A poor person stays poor for his קרבנות until the money is really his, even if it will almost surely come.

phrases.english: When his father was dying.
You might have said: most dying people go on to die?
phrases.notes: So you might have thought the son already counts as rich.

phrases.english: It teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case so that it teaches something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since most גוססין die, the son should already count as rich.
steps.terutzMaskana: Until the father actually dies, the son is still poor.

steps.title: His ship at sea bringing ten thousand: he is rich
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the next case: a man whose ship is bringing him great wealth should be rich.
steps.simpleTranslation: His ship is at sea and is bringing him tens of thousands? He is rich!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה and challenges it. If the goods on the ship are his, he already owns them and is rich.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Goods on a ship at sea are still owned by their owner, even before they arrive. So he seems rich right now.

keyTerms.meaning: Ship
Tens of thousands (dinars)

phrases.english: His ship is at sea and is coming to him with tens of thousands,
he is rich!

steps.triggerLanguage: סְפִינָתוֹ בַּיָּם וּבָאָה לוֹ בְּרִיבּוֹאוֹת, עָשִׁיר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the second case in the same line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's case of the ship at sea.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The cargo already belongs to him, so he is rich now.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the ship is rented out to others
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that the ship was leased or rented to other people, so the cargo is theirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is when the ship was leased or rented out to others.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers by narrowing the case. The goods on board belong to the renters, not to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If other people rent the ship, the valuable cargo is theirs. The owner does not have that wealth, so he can still be poor.

keyTerms.meaning: Leased out; the renter pays a fixed amount out of what it brings in
Rented out, for a set money fee

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
When it was leased or rented in the hands of others.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The cargo is his, so he is rich.
steps.terutzMaskana: The cargo belongs to the renters, so it does not make him rich.

steps.title: But he gets rent money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: even if the cargo isn't his, isn't he owed rent?
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't there the rent money?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא. The renters owe him rent, so maybe that makes him rich.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even without the cargo, the owner earns rent from the ship. That money should count toward his wealth.

keyTerms.meaning: Rent; the payment for renting something
'But isn't there...?'; points out something that was left out

phrases.english: But isn't there the rent?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's case of a rented ship.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rent he is owed should make him rich.

steps.title: Rent is only paid at the end
steps.stepSummary: Rent is only paid at the end of the rental, so right now he does not have it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rent is only paid at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that he does not have the rent money yet. It only comes when the rental period is over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the משנה's main idea: only money he already has counts. Rent he will get later does not make him rich now.

keyTerms.meaning: Is paid
At the end

phrases.english: Rent is paid only at the end.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying a known rule (rent is owed only at the end)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rent makes him rich now.
steps.terutzMaskana: He gets the rent only later, so for now he is poor.

steps.title: The ship itself should make him rich
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: forget the cargo and rent; he owns a ship, which is worth a lot!
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him count as rich because of the ship itself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge. Owning a ship is wealth in itself, so he should already be rich.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the cargo isn't his and the rent hasn't come in, the ship is his property right now. That alone should count.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let him get it from...'; asks why another, simpler reason isn't used

phrases.english: But let it come out for him because of the ship!
phrases.notes: Meaning: he owns the ship, so that alone should make him rich.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the rent problem is solved, the גמרא raises a further problem: the ship itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the ship owner stays poor.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ship is valuable property he owns now, so he should be rich.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this? It is רבי אליעזר's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by saying whose view the משנה follows. It will prove this in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that a person's work tools are not counted against him. So the ship, which is how he makes a living, does not make him rich.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Whose view is this?'; matches a teaching to a specific opinion

phrases.english: Whose is this? It is Rabbi Eliezer's,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the משנה to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ship is wealth and should count.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי אליעזר, the tools of a person's trade, like his ship, are not counted.

steps.title: Proof: רבי אליעזר lets a worker keep his work tools
steps.stepSummary: A משנה shows that רבי אליעזר lets a farmer keep his oxen and a donkey driver keep his donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי אליעזר says, if he was a farmer, they leave him his pair of oxen; if a donkey driver, they leave him his donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to prove that רבי אליעזר does not count a person's work tools against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the treasury collects from a person, רבי אליעזר lets him keep what he uses to earn a living. In the same way, the ship is his means of making a living, so it does not make him rich.

keyTerms.meaning: A farmer who plows
His pair (of oxen) used for plowing
A donkey driver

steps.whatToRemember: The ship owner stays poor because the cargo belongs to the renters, the rent comes only at the end, and, according to רבי אליעזר, a person's work tools are not counted.

phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Eliezer says,
phrases.notes: This משנה is about the treasury collecting what a person owes to הקדש.

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיָה אִיכָּר — נוֹתֵן לוֹ צִמְדּוֹ,
phrases.english: if he was a farmer, he gives him his pair of oxen,
phrases.notes: 'He gives him' means the treasurer lets him keep them.

phrases.english: and a donkey driver, he gives him his donkey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the claim of step 16 about רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר does not count a person's work tools as his wealth.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה (ערכין 23b) in which רבי אליעזר lets a farmer keep his oxen and a donkey driver keep his donkey.

steps.title: The age that counts is the age of the person being valued
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that the ערך amount follows the age of the person being valued, not the age of the person who made the vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The years go by the person vowed about. How so? A youth who valued an elder pays an elder's valuation, and an elder who valued a youth pays a youth's valuation.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. Its first rule is that the age used to set the payment is the age of the person being valued.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה's fixed amounts change with age. The משנה says to look only at the age of the person whose ערך was pledged. The age of the person pledging makes no difference.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה; marks the start of the משנה text
The fixed amount the תורה sets for a person, based on age and gender
He made a vow to give someone's ערך
Here: the person the vow is about, meaning the one being valued

steps.confusionAlert: נִידָּר sounds like it means 'the one who vowed,' but here it means the person the vow is about. That is why the youth pays an elder's amount.

phrases.english: MISHNA: The years go by the one vowed about; how so?
A youth who valued an elder
gives the valuation of an elder,
and an elder who valued the youth
gives the valuation of a youth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It is unrelated to the earlier discussion of what a debtor is allowed to keep.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The age bracket used is that of the person being valued, not that of the person vowing.

steps.title: The gender that counts is the gender of the person being valued
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that the male or female amount follows the person being valued, not the person who vowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The valuations go by the one being valued. How so? A man who valued a woman pays a woman's valuation, and a woman who valued a man pays a man's valuation.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its second rule. Whether the male or female amount is paid depends on the person being valued.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works just like the age rule. The תורה's different amounts for men and women depend only on who is being valued. The gender of the person making the vow does not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: Valuations; here, the different amounts set for males and females
The person being valued
How so? It introduces an example

phrases.english: The valuations go by the one valued; how so?
A man who valued the woman
gives the valuation of a woman,
and a woman who valued a man
gives the valuation of a man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second rule of the same משנה. It matches the age rule in Step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The male or female amount follows the gender of the person being valued.

steps.title: The amount is fixed by the age at the time of the vow
steps.stepSummary: If the person being valued moves into an older age bracket before payment, the amount still follows his age when the vow was made.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the valuation goes by the time of the valuation. How so? He valued someone under five, and that person became over five; or under twenty, and he became over twenty. He pays according to the time of the valuation.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its third rule. The age that counts is the age at the moment of the vow, not at the moment of payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each age bracket has a different amount, and a person can pass into a new bracket before the money is paid. The משנה rules that the amount is locked in when the vow is made.

keyTerms.meaning: The time the valuation vow was made
Younger than (a certain age)
Older than / more than

steps.whatToRemember: Three rules of the משנה: the age follows the one valued, the gender follows the one valued, and the age is fixed at the time of the vow.

phrases.english: And the valuation goes by the time of the valuation; how so?
He valued him when he was less than five years old,
and he became more than five years old;
or less than twenty years old,
and he became more than twenty years old
he gives according to the time of the valuation.
phrases.notes: The person pays the amount for the age bracket the other person was in when the vow was made.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third rule of the משנה. It adds a rule about timing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ערך amount is set by the age of the one valued at the time of the vow, even if he is older at the time of payment.

steps.title: A ברייתא compares market-value pledges to valuations
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that דמים (pledges of a person's market value) were compared to ערכין in two ways: the pearl among the poor, and judging a limb by its importance.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The Rabbis taught: You compared דמים to ערכין in the case of a pearl belonging to poor people, and in judging something by its importance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that links דמים to ערכין on certain points. This sets up the next step, where the ברייתא asks whether the link also covers timing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ערכין are fixed amounts set by the תורה. דמים are pledges of what a person would sell for. The ברייתא says דמים follow the ערכין pattern on two points. Value is judged by the item's actual situation, like a pearl that is among poor people. And a vital limb is judged by its importance, so it is valued like the whole person.

keyTerms.meaning: A pledge to give a person's market value
You compared; you linked one law to another
A pearl
Literally 'light ones'; here, poor people
By its importance or significance

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
You compared assessments to valuations,
a pearl belonging to the poor,
phrases.notes: A pearl is valued for where it actually is, among poor people, not for what it might fetch in a city market.

phrases.english: and to judge it by its importance.
phrases.notes: For a limb a person can't live without, the value is the same as the whole person's.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אַתָּה הִקַּשְׁיתָּ דָּמִים לַעֲרָכִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה's last rule, that the amount is fixed at the time of the vow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דמים are compared to ערכין regarding the pearl among the poor and judging a limb by its importance.

steps.title: Maybe valuations should follow payment time, like market-value pledges
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that we might compare ערכין to דמים the other way, so that ערכין would be paid by the value at the time of payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think we should compare ערכין to דמים, so that he pays according to the time of giving.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible idea it is about to reject. If the two are linked, maybe ערכין should copy the דמים timing rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With דמים, you pay what the person is worth when you pay. If the comparison went both ways, ערכין would follow payment time too. That would contradict the משנה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One might think': it introduces an idea that will be rejected
We should compare
The time of payment

phrases.english: One might think we should compare valuations to assessments,
so that he gives according to the time of giving?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the comparison in Step 21 and asks whether it also works in reverse, for timing.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's own possible extension of the היקש between דמים and ערכין: maybe it also covers timing, so that ערכין would be paid by value at the time of payment.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since the ברייתא compared דמים to ערכין, one might think the comparison works in reverse too, so that ערכין copy the דמים rule of paying by the value at the time of payment. The next step rejects this with כְּעֶרְכְּךָ כֵּן יָקוּם.

steps.title: A פסוק shows valuations are fixed at the time of the vow
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'according to your valuation it shall stand' teaches that a ערך is paid only by the time of the valuation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'According to your valuation it shall stand.' He pays only according to the time of the valuation.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the idea from Step 22 by bringing a פסוק. This supports the משנה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word יָקוּם ('shall stand') shows the ערך stays as it was set when the vow was made. So the comparison does not reach timing. דמים follow payment time, while ערכין stay locked at the vow.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The verse teaches': it brings a פסוק as the source
So shall it stand; it stays as it was set

steps.whatToRemember: ערכין are fixed when the vow is made, as the פסוק says, while דמים follow the value at the time of payment.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"According to your valuation it shall stand,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:17

phrases.english: he gives only according to the time of the valuation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion in Step 22 and supports the משנה in Step 20.
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's rule that a ערך is fixed at the time of the vow

steps.title: Boundary ages count with the younger group
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that the thirtieth day, the fifth year and the twentieth year are each treated like the period before them.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The thirtieth day counts like the time before it. The fifth year and the twentieth year count like the time before them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It tells us how to treat a person who is exactly at an age boundary for ערכין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה sets age groups for ערכין: one month to five, five to twenty, twenty to sixty, and sixty and up. The משנה rules that a person who is in the boundary day or year still belongs to the younger group. For example, a child during his fifth year is valued like a child under five.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the period below it, so it counts with the younger group
The thirtieth day of a baby's life

steps.confusionAlert: 'Like below it' does not mean the person is younger. It means that during the boundary year he is still valued at the lower age group's amount.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The thirtieth day is like the time before it,
phrases.notes: Under one month there is no ערך at all, so on the thirtieth day the person who vowed still pays nothing.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנַת חָמֵשׁ וּשְׁנַת עֶשְׂרִים כִּלְמַטָּה מֵהֶם
phrases.english: the fifth year and the twentieth year are like the time before them,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic: how boundary ages are counted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The thirtieth day and the fifth and twentieth years are counted with the younger age group.

steps.title: Learning the rule from the sixtieth year
steps.stepSummary: The משנה brings a פסוק about 'sixty and up' and learns from it that every boundary year counts like the time before it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And if from sixty years old and up.' We learn all the ages from the sixtieth year. Just as the sixtieth year counts like the time before it, so too the fifth and twentieth years count like the time before them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a source for its rule from the פסוק about the sixtieth year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'from sixty and up,' so the new group starts only after sixty. That means during the sixtieth year itself a person is still in the younger group. The משנה copies this pattern onto the fifth and twentieth years.

keyTerms.meaning: And up, beyond that point
We learn (one case from another)

phrases.english: as it is stated: "And if from sixty years old and upward"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:7

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי אָנוּ לְמֵדִים בְּכוּלָּן מִשְׁנַת שִׁשִּׁים
phrases.english: we learn all of them from the sixtieth year:
just as the sixtieth year is like the time before it,

phrases.aramaic: אַף שְׁנַת חָמֵשׁ וּשְׁנַת עֶשְׂרִים כִּלְמַטָּה הֵימֶנָּה.
phrases.english: so too the fifth year and the twentieth year are like the time before them.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וְאִם מִבֶּן שִׁשִּׁים שָׁנָה וָמַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source for the rule in step 24.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that boundary years count with the younger group.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 27:7, 'from sixty years and up,' used as a pattern for the other ages.

steps.title: A stringency cannot teach a leniency
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks how we can learn from the sixtieth year, where the rule makes the person pay more, to the fifth and twentieth years, where the same rule makes him pay less.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? If the תורה made the sixtieth year like the time before it to be strict, should we make the fifth and twentieth years like the time before them to be lenient?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה challenges its own proof. Copying a strict rule to create a lenient result does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man under sixty is valued at fifty סלעים, but over sixty at only fifteen. So keeping the sixtieth year with the younger group makes him pay more, which is strict. At five and twenty the younger group pays less, so the same rule there would be lenient, and a strict source cannot simply teach a lenient result.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? (a challenging question)
To be strict (here: to pay more)
To be lenient (here: to pay less)

phrases.english: Is that so?

phrases.aramaic: אִם עָשָׂה שְׁנַת שִׁשִּׁים כִּלְמַטָּה מִמֶּנָּה לְהַחְמִיר
phrases.english: If it made the sixtieth year like the time before it to be strict,
phrases.notes: Before sixty the ערך is higher, so this makes him pay more.

phrases.english: shall we make the fifth year and the twentieth year
like the time before them to be lenient?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵן? אִם עָשָׂה שְׁנַת שִׁשִּׁים כִּלְמַטָּה מִמֶּנָּה לְהַחְמִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof of step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: Learning the fifth and twentieth years from the sixtieth year.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source produces a strict result and the target would produce a lenient one, so the comparison does not hold.

steps.title: A גזירה שוה from the word 'year'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה answers that the word 'שנה' appears in both places, making a גזירה שוה that applies whether the result is lenient or strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the פסוק says 'year' and 'year' for a גזירה שוה. Just as the year said about sixty counts like the time before it, so too the year said about five and twenty counts like the time before it, whether to be lenient or strict.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה replaces its logical comparison with a גזירה שוה, which does not depend on whether the result is strict or lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain comparison can be broken by pointing out a difference, like strict versus lenient. A גזירה שוה is a תורה link through a shared word, so it carries the rule over no matter what the outcome is. That is why the משנה adds 'whether lenient or strict.'

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק comes to teach
A link between two פסוקים that share the same word
Whether it makes things easier or stricter

steps.whatToRemember: Boundary years count with the younger group. This is learned through a גזירה שוה of 'שנה' 'שנה,' which works both for leniency and for stringency.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse says "year" and "year" for a verbal analogy:
phrases.notes: The word 'year' appears with the fifth and twentieth years (ויקרא 27:3–6) and with the sixtieth year (ויקרא 27:7).

phrases.aramaic: מָה שָׁנָה הָאֲמוּרָה בִּשְׁנַת שִׁשִּׁים כִּלְמַטָּה
phrases.english: just as the year stated about the sixtieth year is like the time before it,

phrases.aramaic: אַף שָׁנָה הָאֲמוּרָה מִשְׁנַת חָמֵשׁ וּשְׁנַת עֶשְׂרִים
phrases.english: so too the year stated about the fifth year and the twentieth year
is like the time before it,
whether to be lenient or to be strict.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר שָׁנָה שָׁנָה לִגְזֵירָה שָׁוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces a logical comparison with a גזירה שוה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule came from a simple comparison to sixty, which fails because strict and lenient results differ.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule comes from a גזירה שוה of 'שנה,' which applies whether the result is lenient or strict.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: a month and a day past the year
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר holds that a person moves to the older group only once he is a month and a day past the boundary year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: the person stays in the younger group until he is one month and one day beyond those years.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר adds his own view and stretches the boundary even further.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the earlier opinion, the person moves up as soon as the boundary year ends. רבי אליעזר says he stays in the younger group for an extra month and a day after the boundary year.

keyTerms.meaning: Beyond those years
One month and one day

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
until they are beyond the years
phrases.notes: He means the fifth, twentieth and sixtieth years.

phrases.english: by a month and one day.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: עֵד שֶׁיְּהוּ יְתֵירוֹת עַל הַשָּׁנִים חֹדֶשׁ וְיוֹם אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second opinion on when a person moves up a group.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The person stays in the younger group until a month and a day past the boundary year.

steps.title: The גזירה שוה must be built on extra words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the משנה's גזירה שוה must be מופנה, because otherwise the strict-versus-lenient question could still break it.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It is 'free,' because if it were not free, one could refute it the way we refuted the comparison.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה's answer really works. The גזירה שוה must come from words the פסוק did not need.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה from words the פסוק needs for their plain meaning can still be knocked down by logic. Then the old question about strict and lenient results would break it too. Only a מופנה גזירה שוה, built on extra words, is safe from that question.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
'Free': built on words the פסוק does not otherwise need
To refute, to knock down by logic

steps.confusionAlert: A גזירה שוה is not automatically protected from logical questions. Only one made from extra words is protected.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
It is free,
phrases.notes: The words 'year' used for the גזירה שוה are not needed for anything else in the פסוק.

phrases.english: for if it were not free,
one could refute it as we refuted it.
phrases.notes: This points back to the משנה's question: a strict result cannot teach a lenient one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the answer of step 27 survives the question of step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גזירה שוה of 'שנה' must be מופנה, or the משנה's question could refute it.

steps.title: Both words 'year' are extra
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא confirms that both mentions of 'שנה' are extra, so the גזירה שוה is fully מופנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both the first 'year' and the second 'year' are written as extra words.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that the גזירה שוה really is מופנה. Both words 'year' are extra in their פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the word 'year' is extra both in the source (sixty) and in the target (five and twenty), the link is solid on both sides. So the strict-versus-lenient question cannot break it, and the משנה's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Extra, more than needed
Are written (in the פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's גזירה שוה works because both words 'שנה' are extra. That makes it מופנה and protects it from the question that a strict rule cannot teach a lenient one.

phrases.english: "Year" and "year" are written as extra words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the claim of step 29 that the גזירה שוה is מופנה.
steps.raayaObject: That the גזירה שוה of 'שנה' is מופנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Both mentions of 'שנה' in the פסוקים of ערכין are extra.

steps.title: Does the משנה disagree with רבי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that our משנה cannot follow רבי. רבי holds that 'עד' includes the last item, so he would not need a גזירה שוה to include the boundary year.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say our משנה does not follow רבי. If it followed רבי, there is a problem: he holds that 'until' means 'until and including.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible problem. Our משנה may not fit with רבי's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ערכין פסוקים say 'from five years until twenty.' The משנה needed a גזירה שוה to put the twentieth year in the younger group. רבי reads 'עד' as including the endpoint, so for him the פסוק already does this, and the גזירה שוה looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say; the גמרא is suggesting a possible conclusion
'Until' means until and including; the endpoint counts
Not in line with (a certain sage's opinion)

steps.confusionAlert: 'עד בכלל' does not mean the count stops before the endpoint. It means the endpoint itself is included.

phrases.english: Let us say our mishna is not in line with Rabbi,
for if it were Rabbi,
doesn't he say that "until" means until and including?
phrases.notes: The ערכין פסוקים say 'until twenty' and 'until five' (ויקרא 27:3-6), so for רבי those years are already included.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the גזירה שוה from steps 27-30 and asks whether it is needed according to רבי
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's need for a גזירה שוה to include the boundary years
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי, 'עד' already includes the endpoint, so the גזירה שוה adds nothing. That suggests the משנה follows a different view.

steps.title: The source for רבי's rule: the seven days of פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא on the פסוק 'from the first day until the seventh day.' It opens with the possible mistaken reading that neither the first day nor the seventh day is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'From the first day until the seventh day.' One might think this means starting after the first day, so the first day is not included, and stopping before the seventh day, so the seventh day is not included.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting the source for רבי's rule that 'עד' includes the endpoint. Here it only sets up the possible wrong reading; the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא tests the words 'from' and 'until' in the פסוק about חמץ. It first suggests that both edge days might be left out. This prepares for showing, later, that רבי reads the endpoint as included.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought; it introduces a possible reading that will be tested
The first day (of פסח)
The seventh day (of פסח)

phrases.english: As it is taught: "From the first day until the seventh day,"
phrases.notes: שמות 12:15, about the punishment for eating חמץ on פסח.

phrases.english: one might think: from the first, but the first is not included,
until the seventh, but the seventh is not included,

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: מִיּוֹם הָרִאשׁוֹן וְעַד יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the view of רבי cited in step 31
steps.raayaObject: רבי's rule that 'עד' means until and including
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on שמות 12:15, the seven days of eating no חמץ
